title: Finite coefficient encoding identifies the canonical exchange arrows
statement: Let A be a finite discrete commutative ring, R a condensed commutative ring, e:R ≅ A_cont a ring-object isomorphism, and E_T normalized section-action encodings. Let F_T be the fixed-scalar coefficient encoding [def-sfb-finite-coefficient-operation-encoding]. For any chosen Cartesian square X' -> X, Y' -> Y and any unbounded internal R_X-module complex K, the arrow F_Y'(Ex_internal(K)) is isomorphic in the arrow category to the ordinary fixed-A pro-etale exchange at F_X(K). Both exchange arrows are the published unit--canonical pullback square--counit mates. No properness, qcqs, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility is assumed.

source.place: Coefficient transport and clauses (2)--(3), canonical-map identifications.

proof.text: Obtain the family P of coefficient inverse-image comparisons and its composition equation from lem-sfb-finite-coefficient-pullback-encoding. Equality transport in the scheme-morphism argument gives compatibility of P with the middle equality in the square. Apply composition_square_aux to the two paths p′;g and g′;p. Its two hypotheses are exactly the two composition equations for P. This yields the forward inverse-image comparison cube for the published internal and ordinary square isomorphisms.

Define the two direct-image comparisons as the actual mates of (P_p)^(-1) and (P_p′)^(-1), under the published internal and ordinary total-derived adjunctions. Apply isIso_mateEquiv_of_isEquivalence_of_fullyFaithful: each coefficientEncoding is an equivalence, so both mates are natural isomorphisms. This avoids any separate right-derived/K-injective comparison theorem.

Both published exchange arrows are the actual mates of their inverse-image square comparisons. Their counit equations and the counit equations for the two direct-image mates are mateEquiv_counit. Apply coefficient_exchange_of_counit_at to the cube from step 1. Form the source isomorphism as P_g followed by the ordinary pullback of the p direct-image mate, and the target isomorphism as the p′ direct-image mate followed by the ordinary direct image of P_g′. The resulting rectangle, reversed, is Arrow.isoMk's compatibility equation. This constructs the requested arrow isomorphism on the original arbitrary unbounded K, without geometric finiteness or invertibility assumptions on exchange.

proof_origin.place: Canonical-map transport in clause (2); inverse-image composition cancellation and proved coefficient mate calculus.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteCoefficientExchangeEncoding
    (e : Mon.mk R ≅ Mon.mk (coefficient A))
    (E : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Encoding A T)
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {p' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {p : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare g' p' p g)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj R X))) :
    Nonempty (Arrow.mk ((coefficientEncoding A e Y' (E Y')).map
        ((CondensedRing.finiteProperExchange R sq.toCommSq).app K)) ≅
      Arrow.mk ((ProEtale.derivedBaseChangeMap
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) sq.toCommSq).app
          ((coefficientEncoding A e X (E X)).obj K)))
